Research Question: Does Qwen3-8B show repeatable, grounded multi-step successes and policy failures on state-changing development tasks under a fixed budget?
Hypothesis: At least four of twenty nonempty-reference tasks succeed and at least four fail, with grounded multi-step success and repeatable policy-attributable failures
Independent Variable: B0 fixed policy; an optional B1 changes only general task/tool instructions after review
Evidence Gate: See gate object; no-op reward cannot alone establish qualification; inspect raw trajectories and attribution
Cost Bound: Candidate pilot total RMB 80 using an unverified placeholder price; actual provider quote and every experiment over RMB 30 require approval
Failure Branch: Retain invalid runs, diagnose interface versus policy versus task issues, report branch to user; do not automatically enlarge model/context/seeds or train
B0_prompt: Official task system and user messages; no task-specific additions
B1_addition: Complete the user's task with the available tools. Ground identifiers in the user's request or observed tool results. Inspect state when required to decide whether an action is appropriate. Use returned errors to correct the next action and avoid repeating a call without new evidence. Report completion only when supported by the observed outcome.
required_before_rental: User decision about unqualified composition-generalization scope
Actual provider quote and bounded experiment approval
